text: According to this book, a passing gravitational wave directly accelerates an isolated free-falling test mass in that mass's own local inertial frame.
explanation: False. The book explicitly says a gravitational wave does not directly accelerate a free-falling test mass — in its local inertial frame it remains at rest to first order. What the wave changes is the proper distance between two nearby masses, δL/L = ½h_+, which is the quantity LIGO measures. The metric perturbation h_μν is not a Newtonian force.
